title: How a Ceiling Fan Works in 60 Seconds 🌀🏠 #shorts
description:
A ceiling fan doesn't make the room colder, it cools you. A capacitor helps the motor create a rotating magnetic field, an outer rotor spins the tilted blades, and the moving air speeds up evaporation from your skin. Flip the direction in winter to gently push warm air down. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#ceilingfan #homehacks #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A ceiling fan doesn't cool the room at all. It *cools you*.

steps.label: Motor
steps.text: Inside, a *capacitor* shifts the current so the coils make a *rotating* magnetic field.

steps.label: Rotor
steps.text: That field drags the *outer rotor* around, and the blades are bolted to it.

steps.label: Blades
steps.text: Each blade is *tilted*, so it scoops air and pushes a column *downward*.

steps.label: Breeze
steps.text: Moving air speeds up *evaporation* from your skin, so you feel *cooler*.

steps.label: Winter
steps.text: Flip it to *clockwise* in winter and it gently pushes *warm air* down.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Spin, push, *breeze*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
